components.description: The source is the provider's own documentation or manifest.
The claimed feature is supported in the current version.
The source describes the behaviour the claim relies on.
The source names the version the support applies to.

api.expected_evidence: The provider's official documentation or capability manifest stating that the current version supports the feature and describing its behaviour.
api.expected_source: Official documentation or a machine-readable capability manifest published by the API provider.
api.insufficient_support: Roadmaps, announcements of future versions, third-party blog posts, or documentation of a different product.
api.name: API capability in the provider's official documentation
api.sufficient_support: The documentation of the current version states or clearly describes the claimed feature as supported.

components.description: The source is published by the certification body that issued the certificate.
The claimed organisation is named as the holder.
The certificate is to the standard the claim names.
The certificate's scope covers the activity the claim names.
The certificate is currently valid - not expired, suspended or withdrawn.

certification.expected_evidence: The certification body's public register entry naming the organisation, the certificate, the standard, the scope and the current status.
certification.expected_source: A public register or directory published by the certification body that issued the certificate.
certification.insufficient_support: Marketing copy, a company's own website, a news article, an unrelated directory, or a register entry for a different organisation, standard or scope.
certification.name: Accredited certification on the certifier's own register
certification.sufficient_support: The register identifies the claimed organisation and a certificate to the claimed standard whose scope covers the claim and which is currently valid.

components.description: The source is published by the regulator or licensing authority.
A licence of the claimed kind is recorded for the company.
The licence covers the service the claim names.

license.expected_evidence: A public regulator or licensing authority page identifying the company, the relevant licence, the service category and its current status.
license.expected_source: The public register of the regulator or licensing authority.
license.insufficient_support: Marketing copy, an unrelated directory, an old cached article, or a page that mentions the company without establishing the licence.
license.name: Active licence on the regulator's public register
license.sufficient_support: The source identifies the claimed entity and licence and shows that the licence is currently active for the claimed service.
